Method of Attack: Encrypts files with .zzzzz extension after infection
Delivered via emails pretending to be order receipts with ZIP attachments containing JS files
JS file downloads and executes encrypted DLL renamed with non-dll extension (e.g., .TDB)
DLL executed using legitimate Windows program Rundll32.exe to install ransomware
Encrypts targeted file extensions by scrambling file names and appending .zzzzz
Attempts to remove Shadow Volume Copies to prevent recovery
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with ZIP attachments containing malicious JS files
Indicators of Compromise: DLL files with non-dll extensions such as .TDB executed via Rundll32.exe
Emails with subject 'Order #[random_numbers]' and attachment named like order_[target_name].zip
